title: Tiling quotes, levels and defect boundaries
audience: Tilers who quote tiling work and manage defect boundaries with clients
learningOutcomes: Write a tiling quote that states the scope, the substrate preparation, the tile and the exclusions.
Identify the defect boundary between the tiler's work and the substrate or waterproofing that is excluded.
Check the licence threshold for tiling work before quoting.

instruction.heading: What the quote has to state
instruction.body: A tiling quote defines the job, so it has to say what is included as well as what is not. State the areas to be tiled, the tile and who supplies it, the substrate preparation that is included, the adhesive, the grout and any sealing, the layout pattern and the cuts, the waste allowance, access and working hours, and the exclusions. Items that are commonly excluded are substrate repairs and levelling, waterproofing, structural work, removal of old floor coverings or tiles, and any testing or removal the job needs for hazardous materials. Where an item is excluded, say so in the quote and offer to price it separately. Do not leave the substrate preparation unstated, because the client will assume it is included.

instruction.heading: Setting a finish standard that can be checked
instruction.body: A finish standard is only useful if it can be measured on site. A client who expects a flat finish over an uneven substrate will be disappointed unless the levelling is included or quoted separately. Tie the standard to the tile and to the substrate. For example, the quote can state that the finish will be measured with a straight edge over a stated length, and that the result will be recorded at handover. The tolerance figures are set for each job and are not given in this lesson. Wording such as perfectly level or flawless cannot be checked, and a dispute then turns on the wording rather than on the work.

instruction.heading: Recording the substrate before tiling
instruction.body: Before any tile goes down, record the substrate as it is found: its flatness, cracks, moisture where it is measured, previous adhesives or coverings, movement joints and any visible water staining. Photograph each area with the client's permission, and include a straight edge or scale in the frame where the photograph is meant to show flatness. Record in writing the substrate condition the client has accepted. This record is what separates a setting defect, which belongs to the tiler, from a substrate defect, which may not. Older floor coverings, mastics and adhesives can contain asbestos. If the job may disturb them, stop and refer the testing and removal to a licensed or competent person before any work starts. The asbestos thresholds are not verified in this lesson.

instruction.heading: Defect boundaries and consumer guarantees
instruction.body: Defects that come from the tile, the adhesive, the grout or the setting are the tiler's to put right, and the quote and the record define that boundary. Defects that come from substrate movement, an excluded waterproofing system, a previous trade or another unrelated cause sit outside the tiler's work, and they must be recorded with evidence. Whether a quote exclusion limits a consumer guarantee claim is a legal question, and this lesson does not settle it. The ACCC business guidance sets out three service guarantees: care and skill, suitability for a stated purpose, and completion within a reasonable time where no time was agreed. The same page states that a trader's own words or conduct cannot switch these basic rights off. The NSW Government notes that the guarantees operate separately from any warranty a trader gives.

instruction.heading: Variations and written approval
instruction.body: A variation is any change to the agreed scope, such as extra levelling, a changed tile, an additional cut pattern or a substrate problem found during the work. Price each variation, describe what it adds and what it leaves out, and get the client's written approval before the work is done. Keep each variation with the quote and the substrate record. A verbal approval for an extra area is the most common source of a dispute about who pays, so the record should be complete before the work starts.

instruction.heading: Checking the licence position before quoting
instruction.body: The licence position depends on the state, the value of the job and the trades involved, so check it before the quote is issued, and check again if the scope grows. In New South Wales, the tiling page sets out a contractor licence or supervisor certificate for work valued above a threshold that includes GST, and it lists waterproofing of wet areas before tiling among the covered work. In Victoria, a job involving only one listed trade, including wall and floor tiling, does not need building practitioner registration, but combining skills on one job does. In Queensland, wall and floor tiling is a QBCC licence class. The page gives a $3,300 limit for incidental work, and the page read did not give a separate tiling dollar threshold. In South Australia, anyone carrying on business as a building work contractor needs the right licence. The guide sets no dollar threshold and does not name tiling.

procedure: Inspect the area and record the substrate condition, with dated photographs taken with the client's consent, before any quote is issued.
Check the licence position for the state, the job value (including GST where the state counts it) and the trades involved, and note the result on the file.
Write the quote with the scope, substrate preparation, tile, adhesive, grout, any sealing, and the exclusions stated as included or excluded.
State the finish standard in a checkable form, such as a straight-edge tolerance over a stated length, and say how it will be measured at handover.
Obtain the client's written acceptance of the recorded substrate condition and the exclusions.
For each variation, price it, describe what it adds and what it leaves out, and obtain written approval before it is performed.
File the quote, the substrate record, the licence check, the approvals and any advice received about exclusions with the job file.

workedExamples.situation: A client complains that a newly tiled floor is not level. The substrate was visibly uneven before tiling, the levelling was excluded in the signed quote, and the client's own photographs show the same high spot that was recorded before work started.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Who is responsible for the unevenness, and what do you offer?
workedExamples.reasoning: The unevenness came from the substrate. The quote excluded levelling, and the substrate was recorded and photographed before tiling. Show the before photographs, the signed exclusion and the record of the high spot. Offer to quote the levelling as a separate variation, to be approved in writing before the work. Whether the exclusion would hold against a consumer guarantee claim is not settled by this lesson, so take advice before refusing responsibility outright, and keep the discussion to the record.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) A client asks you to tile a shower recess and says the waterproofing was done by someone else about two years ago. You cannot see the membrane.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you quote the tiling, and what do you say about the waterproofing?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not quote or accept responsibility for the waterproofing unless it is within your scope and you are authorised to do it. The NSW tiling page lists waterproofing of wet areas before tiling as covered tiling work, so the boundary has to be stated in the quote. Record the condition you can see, state that the membrane is excluded and was not verified, and ask the client for the earlier waterproofing record. Where the client wants the membrane checked, recommend a licensed or qualified waterproofer for that check and keep the two scopes separate.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) In New South Wales, a wall-tiling quote totals labour and materials that sit close to the $5,000 threshold, GST included. The client asks you to split the price across two invoices so that it stays under the threshold.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is splitting the job an acceptable way to handle the threshold?
workedExamples.reasoning: Lesson guidance, not an official requirement: the NSW tiling page does not address splitting a job across invoices. Price the whole scope as one job and check the total, including GST, against the threshold. As lesson guidance, splitting one scope of work into parts to stay under a threshold is not a method this lesson supports. If the position is unclear, confirm it with Building Commission NSW before the quote is issued, and record the calculation and the answer with the quote. This lesson does not grant a licence, and it does not confirm the outcome for any particular job.

equipmentAndPpe: Quote template with scope, substrate preparation, materials and exclusions
Straight edge, spirit level and lippage gauge for the finish standard
Camera or phone for substrate photographs, used only with the client's consent
Moisture meter where the adhesive or underlay data sheet requires a reading
Tape measure and a printed licence-check record for the job file
Site PPE as set by the tiling lessons when the substrate is inspected on site (the quote itself needs no PPE)

commonErrors.error: Quoting tile without stating the substrate preparation or the levelling as included or excluded.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the substrate preparation and levelling into the quote as included or excluded, and get the client's acceptance in writing.

commonErrors.error: Accepting responsibility for a substrate defect without evidence.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the substrate condition with dated photographs before tiling, and show that record when a defect is raised.

commonErrors.error: Quoting waterproofing or structural work without the scope or the authority to do it.
commonErrors.prevention: State the waterproofing and structural work as excluded unless it is in your scope, and refer it to a qualified person.

commonErrors.error: Using vague finish wording such as flawless or perfectly level.
commonErrors.prevention: Tie the finish to a stated, measurable tolerance and the method of measurement.

commonErrors.error: Approving or starting a variation on a verbal instruction.
commonErrors.prevention: Price the variation and obtain the client's written approval before the work is performed.

commonErrors.error: Quoting without checking the state threshold or the value of the whole job.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the licence position for the state and the whole job value before the quote is issued, and record the check.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: New South Wales: the NSW Government page says a contractor licence or qualified supervisor certificate is needed for wall and floor tiling work valued at more than $5,000 in labour and materials, including GST. Floating floors are not named on that page.

Victoria: the Consumer Victoria page says a job involving only one listed trade, including wall and floor tiling, does not need registration, and that combining skills on one job requires registration.

Queensland: wall and floor tiling is a QBCC licence class. The page gives a $3,300 limit for incidental work, and it does not give a separate tiling dollar threshold in the text read. The page shows last reviewed and last published dates of 31 August 2021 (footer shows 2023; fee text refers to 1 July 2026), so current fees and rules must be checked with the QBCC. The $3,300 incidental-work figure is not dated and is not confirmed by an official source.

South Australia: the guide requires the right licence for anyone carrying on business as a building work contractor. It sets no dollar threshold for licensing and does not name tiling. No date is shown on the guide.

This lesson does not grant a licence for tiling or for floating floors in any state or territory. Floating floors are not named on the NSW or QBCC tiling pages; the licence position is not confirmed by an official source.

Asbestos may be present in older floor coverings, mastics and adhesives. Asbestos removal is licensed work in each state and territory, and the classes and thresholds differ. Refer any suspected material to the state regulator or a licensed removalist before it is disturbed.
Completing this lesson does not give a tiling licence, or authority to quote waterproofing or structural work.
This lesson gives no legal advice on exclusion clauses.

qualityStandard: The quote states the scope, the substrate preparation, the materials, the exclusions and a finish standard that can be measured.
The substrate condition is recorded with dated photographs, taken with consent, before tiling starts.
The client has accepted the recorded substrate condition and the exclusions in writing.
Each variation is priced and approved in writing before it is performed.
The licence position for the state and the job value was checked before the quote was issued.
documentationEvidence: Signed tiling quote with scope, exclusions and finish standard
Licence position check, with the state, job value (including GST where relevant) and the result
Substrate condition record with dated photographs
Variation records with written client approval
Note of any advice taken about exclusions or the licence position
summary: Quote the substrate preparation, levelling, waterproofing position and exclusions in writing.
Record the substrate condition with dated photographs before tiling, to separate setting defects from substrate defects.
Approve every variation in writing before the extra work is done.
Check the state position and the whole job value, including GST where relevant, before quoting.

knowledgeChecks.question: A tiled floor is not level, and the substrate was uneven and excluded from the quote. What is the best response?
options: Accept full responsibility and re-tile the whole floor free of charge for the client and the house
Show the before photographs and the exclusion, and offer levelling as a separate approved variation
Blame the client without showing any record of the work, the photos, the quote or the job
Refuse to discuss it at all with the client, the owner, the agent, the builder or the crew

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should substrate condition be photographed and recorded before tiling?
options: To make the job look more professional to the client and the owner
Because the tile manufacturer requires it and nothing else
To separate setting defects from substrate defects if a dispute arises
It is not necessary if the substrate looks sound to the eye

knowledgeChecks.question: A quote excludes levelling, and the client later makes a defect claim. What is the most accurate statement?
options: The exclusion always removes any consumer guarantee the client has under the law, the contract and the quote
A trader's own words cannot switch off the basic consumer rights, so take advice on the effect of the exclusion
Consumer guarantees never apply to services, only to goods bought from a shop in the city centre or the mall nearby
Once a quote is signed, the work cannot be questioned by the client at any stage of the job or after
